headline: Gaibandha's 'One Taka Teacher' receives state honor and pension
summary: Lutfur Rahman has spent 52 years teaching underprivileged children for just one taka, earning him national recognition.
details: Lutfur Rahman, known as the 'One Taka Teacher' of Gaibandha, has been awarded a state honor for his lifelong dedication to education.
For 52 years, he has taught underprivileged children in his community for a nominal fee of only one taka.
Despite not being a formal institutional teacher, the government has recognized his contribution and announced a retirement pension for him.
His commitment to ensuring that poverty does not hinder a child's education has earned him widespread respect across the country.

caption:
Teaching for just 1 taka for 52 years. Now, the state honors the 'One Taka Teacher'.

Lutfur Rahman, known as the 'One Taka Teacher' of Gaibandha, has been awarded a state honor for his lifelong dedication to education.

For 52 years, he has taught underprivileged children in his community for a nominal fee of only one taka.

Despite not being a formal institutional teacher, the government has recognized his contribution and announced a retirement pension for him.

His commitment to ensuring that poverty does not hinder a child's education has earned him widespread respect across the country.

The award serves as a recognition of his selfless service to the underprivileged children of Gaibandha.

headline: Ctg: 6 policemen arrested for yaba trade in 8 months
summary: Over 15 others suspended for embezzling seized drugs. Officials warn that some officers use their identity to bypass checkpoints.
details: Six policemen were arrested in six separate incidents across Chattogram district between August 2025 and April this year for their involvement in yaba smuggling.
More than 15 other police personnel have been suspended for allegedly embezzling yaba tablets seized at checkpoints.
In a recent case, nine CMP personnel were suspended after allegedly embezzling around 1 lakh yaba tablets recovered from a member of Cox’s Bazar District Police.
Senior officials revealed that the identities of involved officers were sometimes deliberately omitted from FIRs to protect the force's image, and some information was kept from the media.
Traffickers pay commissions on a per-tablet basis, luring some officers into the syndicate because they can pass through checkpoints without suspicion.
A joint network is operating to smuggle yaba from Cox’s Bazar through Chattogram to Dhaka and other parts of the country.
CMP Commissioner Hasan Md Showkat Ali and Chattogram District SP Masud Alam have stated that no one will be spared regardless of their identity.
caption:
Six policemen arrested, 15+ suspended. A drug smuggling syndicate is infiltrating the police force in Chattogram.

Six policemen were arrested in six separate incidents across Chattogram district between August 2025 and April this year for their involvement in yaba smuggling.

More than 15 other police personnel have been suspended for allegedly embezzling yaba tablets seized at checkpoints.

In a recent case, nine CMP personnel were suspended after allegedly embezzling around 1 lakh yaba tablets recovered from a member of Cox’s Bazar District Police.

Senior officials revealed that the identities of involved officers were sometimes deliberately omitted from FIRs to protect the force's image, and some information was kept from the media.

Traffickers pay commissions on a per-tablet basis, luring some officers into the syndicate because they can pass through checkpoints without suspicion.

A joint network is operating to smuggle yaba from Cox’s Bazar through Chattogram to Dhaka and other parts of the country.

CMP Commissioner Hasan Md Showkat Ali and Chattogram District SP Masud Alam have stated that no one will be spared regardless of their identity.
